_about: A zero-setup demo memory for 'Orchard', a fictional local-first notes app. Every row has an explicit id + created_at so the demo is fully deterministic. Loaded by project_memory.demo.build_demo().

episodes.content: We chose SQLite over Postgres for Orchard's store because the app is local-first and must run with zero ops on a user's machine.
We chose SQLite FTS5 + BM25 for note search so search works fully offline with no external service.
Gotcha: FTS5 external-content triggers crash on NULL columns; every trigger value must be coalesced to '' or inserts fail silently.
Insight: most note recall is recency-biased — users look for what they touched this week, so created_at ordering matters more than raw relevance.
Invariant: note search must keep working with no network. Any feature that adds a hard network dependency to search is rejected.
Gotcha: created_at was stored as a naive local datetime, so notes reordered when the user changed timezones. Fixed by storing UTC ISO-8601 everywhere.
We decided to defer multi-user auth to v2; v1 is single-user local, so auth is not on the critical path.
Milestone: Orchard v0.1 shipped — local notes, offline FTS5 search, UTC timestamps.

facts.claim: SQLite is Orchard's store of record.

facts.reason: FTS5 + BM25 over local rows; no network in the search path.

facts.claim: All timestamps are stored as UTC ISO-8601.
facts.reason: A naive-local created_at reordered notes across timezone changes.

facts.claim: From a security perspective, storing access tokens in plaintext is an unacceptable risk.
facts.reason: A single DB leak would expose every user's live sessions.

facts.claim: From a business perspective, the legacy plaintext token store was cheap and worked fine.
facts.reason: It shipped on time and never caused a support ticket.
